summary.name: ClashX
summary.one_liner: ClashX is a macOS proxy tool (rule-based Clash client) whose retained download, setup guide and troubleshooting page is kept online after development shifted to its successor, ClashFX.
use_cases: download a retained ClashX release for macOS
set up a subscription config in ClashX
troubleshoot failed connections or subscription updates
migrate a ClashX configuration to ClashFX
route domestic traffic direct and foreign traffic via proxy
summary.what_it_does: The page hosts ClashX retained version v1.140.0, setup steps (install the dmg from GitHub, paste a subscription link, choose rule mode and enable system proxy) and troubleshooting tips for common issues such as expired subscriptions, system proxy not set, and node latency. It lists a changelog from v1.119.0 to v1.140.0, covering macOS Sequoia fixes, Sparkle update key fixes, and a Dashboard switch to MetaCubeX/Yacd-meta. It describes ClashX as a Go-based, low-memory macOS client with rule-based routing and traffic monitoring. The page states that ClashX is no longer maintained and that development has moved to ClashFX, whose core features are free while a Pro tier is not yet available for purchase.
notable: Retained ClashX v1.140.0 download sourced only from official GitHub releases, with setup and troubleshooting guides
Rule-based routing with system proxy and TUN mode options
Page states ClashX is discontinued and points users to ClashFX; back up config before migrating
Go-based, Apple Silicon optimized, GPL-3.0 licensed per the page
caveats: ClashX is no longer maintained; the page only keeps historical downloads and guides
ClashFX Pro is not yet available for purchase; only its core features are free
Third-party proxy nodes must be from trusted sources, per the page's own risk notice
